ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), including International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017 (as amended); Money Laundering (Prevention) Regulations 2018; International Companies Regulations 1998; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Directives; Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) supervision guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles of the originating company (if a corporate shareholder) or notarised proposed Memorandum and Articles in Chinese with English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: P.R.C. Notary Public / Provincial Justice Bureau and Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised passport copies and residential address proof for each shareholder, director, officer and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: P.R.C. Notary Public and Public Security Bureau; authenticated by P.R.C. Ministry of Foreign Affairs or provincial Foreign Affairs Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration, source of wealth statement, source of funds statement, and AML/KYC questionnaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoan Registered Agent / Compliance Officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation only in Samoa; no apostille required for domestic Samoan documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent registry extract of the parent/corporate beneficial owner from its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry or designated competent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, authorised signatories and UBOs against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Samoa's domestic sanctions and terrorism-financing list. Foreign Politically Exposed Persons are subject to enhanced due diligence in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12 and the Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT guidance. Screening records, including negative hits, are required to be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (SICR), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Apia, Samoa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official languages are English and Samoan. An International Company name must be submitted in Roman/Latin script. A Chinese-character name may be adopted as a supplementary foreign-language name provided that a Romanised transliteration and an English/Samoan translation are filed with the Registered Agent and the Registry. Chinese-only articles may be used internally, but a certified English translation must accompany all filings for Registry purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the applicant through its licensed Registered Agent may file a written appeal with the Samoa International Companies Registry within 21 calendar days of the refusal notice. The written appeal must set out the proposed name, search results, compliance analysis and any ministerial consent obtained. The Registrar must issue a decision within 14 calendar days. An unfavourable decision may be referred to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour for administrative review, followed by judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance 1961 and the International Companies Act 1987.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible for the statutory registered office. The International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the office of its licensed Registered Agent. For a wholly offshore liquor export distribution structure where goods never enter Samoa, no additional physical commercial premises are required in Samoa, and operational substance may be maintained in the origin or destination markets.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection of a standard offshore International Company is below 5%. However, the Registered Agent's premises and client records are subject to regulatory inspection by the Samoa International Finance Authority and the Central Bank of Samoa.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Sections 8-17) as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2009; Business Licenses Act 1998; Sale of Liquor Act 2007; Planning and Urban Management Act 2004
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form ICA-1 - Application for Incorporation of an International Company, accompanied by the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, filed under Section 8 of the International Companies Act 1987
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The International Companies Act 1987 permits incorporation with one subscriber and one share (with or without par value). No escrow deposit, notarized capital declaration, or banker's certificate is required as a condition precedent.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED that the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Company, as filed with the Registrar of International Companies, be and are hereby adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that the initial subscriber share be allotted, issued, and recorded as fully paid. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office within Samoa, as stated in the incorporation filing, is adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Director Name] be appointed as the sole Director and [Secretary Name] as the Corporate Secretary. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Director is authorized to execute all statutory returns, license applications, bank account forms, and liquor-export permits on behalf of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER that corporate books, registers, and the common seal be established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name reservation application to SIFA either through the licensed Registered Agent or directly at the SIFA counter. The proposed name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', or another approved designator and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoan company name. SIFA will conduct an internal registry search and issue a written name reservation confirmation.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Request Form (Form ICA-NR)
Letter of authorization from the proposed subscriber
Passport copy of the proposed subscriber or beneficial owner (AML verification)
Proof of Registered Agent appointment, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for conflict, the applicant may immediately re-file with an alternative name or submit a notarized letter of consent from the holder of the conflicting name. A written reconsideration request may be filed with the Registrar within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent or Notary Public, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFA-licensed Registered Agent to draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987, including permitted objects covering international wholesale distribution of alcoholic beverages. The sole subscriber must execute the M&A before the Registered Agent or a Notary Public. The M&A must state the authorized share capital, registered office clause, and any permitted restrictions, and must be dated and witnessed.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber consent and signature block page
Registered Agent Letter of Consent
Identity and address verification of the subscriber and ultimate beneficial owner
AML/KYC questionnaire as required by SIFA policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA later identifies drafting deficiencies, the Registered Agent will prepare amended M&A and re-execute with the subscriber. Corrections made within the 14-day SIFA notice period incur no penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form ICA-1 together with the executed M&A, the written consents of the first director and secretary, and the Registered Agent's consent for the registered office. Pay the statutory filing fee of USD 100 via bank draft or SIFA-approved electronic transfer. SIFA will verify the documents, run AML checks on the officers, and proceed to issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form ICA-1 - Application for Incorporation
Two executed copies of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to Act as Director (signed by first director)
Consent to Act as Secretary (signed by first secretary)
Consent of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Evidence of payment of statutory filing fee
AML/KYC pack for directors, secretary, and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a requisition for further information, the Registered Agent must respond within 21 days. Failure to respond results in abandonment of the application, which may be cured by fresh filing with the applicable fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful verification, SIFA will issue the Certificate of Incorporation under the seal of the Registrar, together with two certified copies of the M&A. The Registered Agent will collect the certificate and deliver the certified originals to the Company. The Company is deemed incorporated as of the date on the certificate and the registered office is legally effective.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgment of receipt of Certificate of Incorporation
Payment receipt for incorporation filing fee
Certified true copies of the filed M&A
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued within the stated SLA, the Registered Agent may escalate in writing to the SIFA management for expedition. Urgent same-day issuance is available upon written request and payment of the expedited fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Establishment of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company, assisted by the Registered Agent, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting and adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering adoption of the M&A, allotment of the subscriber share, confirmation of the registered office, appointment of director and secretary, and authorization of bank account and license applications. Maintain the statutory registers of members, directors, secretaries, and charges at the registered office in Samoa, and issue the share certificate to the sole subscriber.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board Meeting
Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Share certificate stub and Register of Members entry
Register of Directors and Secretaries
Notarized board resolution for bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer consent is found defective, the board may adopt a written ratification resolution and file a Notice of Change of Director or Secretary with SIFA within 30 days without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Notification and Business License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licensing Division, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file the Business License application under the Business Licenses Act 1998 with MCIL, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, M&A, evidence of premises lease, and the First Board Resolution authorizing the application. The application must specify the business activity as 'wholesale export distribution of distilled spirits (Chinese baijiu)' and include the premises address in Samoa. MCIL will verify the application and, upon approval, issue the annual Business License.
required_dossiers: MCIL Business License Application Form (Form BL-1)
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Copy of lease agreement or title deed for the Samoa premises
First Board Resolution authorizing the license application
Passport copies of the director and beneficial owner
Existing or pending Wholesale Liquor License endorsement under the Sale of Liquor Act 2007
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MCIL rejects the Business License application on technical grounds, the applicant may request written reasons and re-submit corrected forms. A refusal of a liquor endorsement may be appealed to the Liquor Licensing Authority within 28 days of the notice of refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licensing Division, Apia, Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License under the Business Licenses Act 1998; Wholesale Liquor License (Export Endorsement) under the Sale of Liquor Act 2007; Customs Export Declaration under the Customs Act 2004

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Apia, Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Minor Scheduled Activity requiring only Project Registration and Development Consent under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; no full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is mandated for bonded wholesale liquor warehousing and export distribution operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge from the warehousing operation; stormwater runoff from the compound must meet the Samoa National Environmental Standards (Total Suspended Solids <= 50 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0, no visible oil sheen). Ethanol vapor and VOC control must be achieved through vapor-sealed container storage, mechanical ventilation, and secondary containment spill pallets for all storage quantities exceeding 200 L of high-proof baijiu.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) validating fire-rated storage for Class IB flammable liquids; Building Occupancy Permit with structural load certification from MCIL Planning Division; Occupational Safety and Health registration and workplace clearance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013, including fire warden training, spill-response capability, and first-aid kit certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), established under the Samoa Revenue Authority Act 2022 as the unified revenue and customs administration (successor to the Ministry for Revenue and the Customs Division); self-service filing via the SRA Tax Administration System (TAS) portal at https://www.sra.gov.ws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Samoa International Company (WS_IC): (1) the licensed registered agent files the incorporation application with the Registrar of International Companies at the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) under the International Companies Act 1987; (2) upon issue of the Certificate of Incorporation, the registered agent lodges SRA Form TIN-01 with the Samoa Revenue Authority, attaching the certified certificate of incorporation, the memorandum and articles of association and the agent's letter of good standing; (3) the SRA issues the company's unique Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) via the TAS portal within 5-10 business days; (4) because the IC is entirely offshore, no income-tax file and no VAGST registration is opened unless the company later elects to carry on a taxable activity in Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box election. The IC is automatically exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, distributions tax, stamp duty and all other Samoan taxes under the International Companies Act 1987, s. 186 (as amended). The only statutory election is an opt-in to the Income Tax Act 2015 regime: an IC that files notice with the SRA that it is carrying on business in Samoa becomes taxable on its Samoa-source income and forfeits the exemption. There is no hybrid-mismatch or disregarded-entity re-characterization election available to an exempt IC other than formal liquidation and re-incorporation as a local company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) imposed under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2003
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WS$ 100,000 (Samoa Tala) value of taxable supplies made in Samoa over any rolling 12-month period; voluntary registration is available where taxable supplies are between WS$ 50,000 and WS$ 100,000; a non-resident IC whose baijiu supply chain (PRC stock to non-resident distributors) never crosses into Samoa has no taxable activity in Samoa and is not registrable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no national clearance-API e-invoicing layer and no digital stamping. Samoa mandates electronic filing and payment of VAGST returns in the SRA TAS portal; domestic point-of-sale receipts must be issued through SRA-approved Electronic Fiscal Devices where applicable; export transactions are cleared through ASYCUDA World (Samoa Customs) and the CusDEC export entry, the validated bill of lading and the VAGST-R1 refund application are digitally cross-matched against the exporter's TAS account before any refund is remitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAGST Act 2003, s. 28: supplies of goods physically exported from Samoa to a place outside Samoa, and long-distance international transport, are zero-rated where the exporter holds documentary proof of export within 30 days of the time of supply. A Samoa IC structured as an offshore spirits wholesaler that sources Chinese baijiu from bonded stock outside Samoa and invoices non-resident distributors by SWIFT wire or letter of credit has no Samoa taxable supply and therefore no VAGST payable; where goods are consolidated or trans-shipped through a Samoan port, the 0% rate applies and the IC may claim refundable input credits (local warehousing, handling and customs-related charges) through the VAGST-R1 refund mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusDEC) lodged through ASYCUDA World; Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from Samoa; Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the licensed commercial bank confirming receipt of export proceeds
Original sales contract and commercial invoice matching description, volume (litres of pure alcohol) and unit price to the CusDEC
SWIFT wire or Letter of Credit documentation matching the remittance certificate and the bank's exchange-control filing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating refund claims are subject to mandatory SRA post-clearance audit and Customs verification. Where false declarations, fictitious exports, circular remittances or forged bills of lading are detected, the SRA claws back the refunded VAGST plus a shortfall penalty of 25%-150% of the tax shortfall (Tax Administration Act 2012), imposes interest at 20% per annum on the clawed-back amount, cancels the exporter's VAGST registration, and may prosecute directors and beneficial owners for tax evasion under TAA 2012, s. 33, with joint and several criminal and civil liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) - Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, exercising statutory exchange control powers under the Exchange Control Act 1976 (as amended) and the Exchange Control Regulations 1983. CBS operates exclusively through designated Authorized Dealers (ADs), which are the licensed commercial banks in Apia. The AD acts as the reporting and approval gateway for all inward/outward remittances, export proceeds verification, and any capital-account transaction involving the Samoan Tala (WST).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The WST is a partially convertible, administered currency without a deep offshore interbank market; conversion is available only through ADs at CBS-published indicative rates. Current-account transactions (trade in goods such as baijiu export, shipping, insurance, distributor commissions) are freely permitted for an International Company (IC) through an AD with underlying commercial documentation. Capital-account flows (initial equity injection, intercompany loans, profit repatriation to non-resident shareholders) require prior CBS exchange-control approval via the AD, or a documented AD exemption for non-resident ICs operating in the Tax-Exempt Zone. Profit remittance from the IC is generally unrestricted once audited financial statements, tax clearance (if any), board resolution, and source-of-funds evidence are filed; practical hurdle is WST liquidity, so USD-denominated accounts and USD settlement are mandatory for the Chinese baijiu trade.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory remittance rule: 100% of export proceeds must be repatriated through an AD in Samoa within a maximum of 90 days from the bill-of-lading date, with the export certificate/electronic customs declaration filed to CBS via the AD. Proceeds invoiced in a foreign currency (USD, and where accepted CNY) may be credited to and retained in an approved foreign-currency account held with the AD; mandatory conversion into WST applies only where the exporter elects WST settlement or operates without an approved foreign-currency account. For a tax-exempt IC, CBS generally permits USD retention to fund onward China supplier payments, provided no net WST conversion is sought; any extension of the 90-day window requires a written CBS exemption submitted by the AD at least 14 days before expiry.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Account + USD/WST Foreign-Currency Account (CBS-registered); segregated Escrow/Collection Account for trade receipts
WST Operational Account; USD account available on application
WST Operational Account only; policy-lending focus; limited IC trade-services appetite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa has no fintech EMI licensing regime; offshore digital banks and EMIs (e.g., UK FCA or Lithuanian-licensed) cannot clear WST, cannot operate local IBANs, and CBS exchange control requires all trade receipts to flow through a Samoan AD. An offshore EMI may only be used as a collection conduit if funds are swept immediately to the BSP/ANZ-class AD account and documented, but most Samoan compliance officers will reject such flows as opaque source-of-funds; therefore, reliance on EMIs is not commercially viable for a baijiu exporter.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or the authorized signatory is mandatory for first-time IC account opening at BSP; a face-to-face interview in Apia (or at a BSP branch in another jurisdiction with video link to Apia) is required. Remote/hybrid onboarding is possible only where the IC is administered by a licensed Samoan International Company & Trust Services Provider, which pre-verifies identity, couriers original notarized documents, and conducts a supervised video KYC interview; non-resident Chinese shareholders/UBOs must independently complete sanctioned-person screening and a video interview witnessed by the AD compliance officer. No fully electronic zero-touch opening is permitted for an IC engaged in regulated spirits export.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is a PRC national with opaque source of wealth or potential PEP/sanctions overlap
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passport copy; independent source-of-wealth statement supported by 12 months of PRC bank statements; corporate registry extract showing direct/holding chain; commercial sanctions and PEP screening report with clear results; sworn declaration of funds origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-proof baijiu export (ISIC 4632 / NAICS 424820) flagged for alcohol excise evasion and PRC cross-border smuggling exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Samoan liquor export licence; PRC importer registration and 食品经营许可证; China Customs HS code registration (2208.90); registered distribution agreements with licensed PRC wholesalers; batch health/sanitary certificates; end-importer and end-use declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party or collection-agent payments from logistics facilitators in China, raising trade-based money laundering (TBML) flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual chain matching each invoiced transaction; signed third-party collection waiver among buyer, agent, and IC; AML risk assessment of the intermediary; transaction monitoring protocol; written commitment prohibiting offsetting or non-contractual settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection classified as capital-account inflow requiring CBS approval
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS exchange-control approval letter or AD exemption confirmation; share subscription agreement; board resolution authorising the injection; SWIFT remittance using purpose code 'CAPI/Equity'; source-of-funds bank statements; certified copy of the IC register of members.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letter of Credit counterparties are PRC banks perceived as high-risk for trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete LC document package (MT700, commercial invoice, clean on-board bill of lading, insurance certificate, certificate of origin, CIQ/fumigation certificate); independent wholesale pricing benchmark for baijiu; customs valuation declaration; EDD report on the issuing bank; annual TBML risk assessment of the trade corridor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity injections must be executed as SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers from the shareholder's account to the IC's BSP USD operational account, using remittance purpose code 'EQUI/CAPI' (equity contribution) and unrestricted memo 'Subscription to WS International Company capital'. The AD will require CBS approval or exemption before crediting; funds must not be commingled with export trade receipts. Mandatory verification pack: share subscription agreement, board resolution, certified member register, identity/source-of-funds documents of the injecting shareholder, and the CBS application or AD waiver. Amounts exceeding USD 100,000 trigger CBS reporting; WST conversion is optional and only if the IC requires local-currency operating liquidity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: (i) Supplier advances and spot purchases of Chinese baijiu, glassware, and packaging: SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'IMPG/Goods' and supporting commercial invoice, purchase contract, import permit, and shipping instructions; no cash or crypto rails accepted. (ii) Bulk distillery procurement from mainland China: irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the AD via SWIFT MT700, payable by sight draft against full document set (bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, inspection certificate, CIQ/fumigation certificate, and Chinese export health permit), typically covering 90% of the first tranche. (iii) Freight, insurance, and logistics: MT103 to carriers or insurers with invoice reference and transport contract; all outbound flows must be reconcilable against CBS export receipt records to demonstrate currency matching and prevent TBML flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST deliverable outright forwards up to 12 months via the AD, fully backed by a confirmed baijiu sales/purchase contract with a 100% maximum hedge ratio of underlying exposure.

USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed with an offshore licensed bank (e.g., Singapore or Hong Kong) only after obtaining prior CBS exchange-control approval through the AD, limited to hedging the Chinese baijiu procurement price.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps between WST/USD/CNY with AD intermediation, permitted solely for matched trade receipts and payables; speculative positions are prohibited under the Exchange Control Regulations 1983.

LC-based structured trade finance (banker's acceptance against LC documents) used as an economical hedging substitute, fixing the USD cost of Chinese baijiu procurement without separate derivative documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return for International Company (Form AR) confirming registered office, registered agent, authorised and issued capital, shareholders, and directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on the incorporation anniversary; submission permitted within 30 calendar days after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% per annum accruing on the unpaid annual government fee; continued non-payment beyond one year from the due date triggers a Registrar show-cause notice and administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Statement endorsed with the Annual Return and evidencing the current register of beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the Annual Return, within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary; interim updates required within 14 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain and confirm the beneficial ownership register constitutes an offence under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), attracting monetary penalties per default and exposing the company to deregistration or restoration proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return (Form ESR) declaring conduct of core income-generating activity and substantial economic presence in Samoa for the financial period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the International Company's financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inadequate substance reporting exposes the company to financial penalties, an economic substance default determination, and mandatory exchange of information with foreign competent tax authorities; persistent default leads to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a private International Company under the International Companies Act 1987; independent audit becomes compulsory only where (i) shareholders elect and resolve that audited financial statements be prepared, (ii) the company is listed or makes public securities offerings, or (iii) the Registrar of International Companies directs an audit on grounds of domestic trading activity or public interest exposure.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) apply to audited financial statements; International Companies not subject to audit must keep proper books and accounting records prepared on a basis consistent with IFRS or a local GAAP framework acceptable to the licensed registered agent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a statutory beneficial ownership register and confirm its content annually in conjunction with the Annual Return; any shareholding transfer that alters beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register immediately and the updated register must be filed with the registered agent and SIFA within 14 days of the transfer, with annual confirmation resubmitted at the next anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Secretaries and Registered Agent
Minute Book of general meetings and director meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per annum, depending on the licensed registered agent's service scope and inclusive of registered office provision and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 per certified audit engagement where an independent audit is voluntarily elected or directed by the Registrar

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% resident corporate income tax rate; 0% effective rate for a compliant Samoa International Company (statutorily exempt on non-Samoan-source income).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory exemption for International Companies under the International Companies Act 2023: exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty on offshore export distribution trading; no branch profits tax; no withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders; no capital gains tax on share disposals. Resident commercial companies qualify for no material tax holidays outside the foreign investment incentive regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form ICA-AR) — filed electronically through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) licensed-registered-agent portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within one month after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (International Companies Act 2023, s.174); the licensed registered agent files on behalf of the IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number, and date of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact English name as registered; no unregistered trade names may be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office in Samoa (full physical address)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be the licensed registered agent's Samoa office; a PO Box alone is insufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent name and licence number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a Samoa-licensed agent at all times; the agent certifies ongoing compliance.
Non-resident directors and shareholders are permitted; provide passport copies and residential addresses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholders, share classes, par value, and issued shares
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited; disclose ultimate beneficial owners for AML/CFT vetting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of business activities and any Samoan-source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no business is carried on in Samoa with Samoan residents, preserving the tax-exempt status.
For a baijiu export wholesaler, select 'Distribution and Service Centre'; state Samoa premises, employees, and local expenditure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual return: WST 100 per month of delinquency plus possible strike-off by the Registrar; false declaration: fine up to WST 10,000 and/or imprisonment; continued non-compliance triggers automatic loss of the tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (MoR Form C) — Ministry for Revenue (MoR) e-Services portal; applicable only where the International Company breaches its exemption or for a resident Samoan trading company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed on or before 31 March following the 31 December year of assessment (within three months of the fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Samoan-source profits if the IC breaches the exemption; attach a source reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: cost of goods sold, freight, insurance, agency commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with invoices and shipping documents; related-party baijiu purchases are subject to arm's-length pricing.
Net assessable profit derived from a Samoan source.
Apply the non-resident company rate to Samoan-source taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Samoan WHT certificates and foreign tax credit computations.
Payment is due within 30 days of assessment; deferral requires a bank guarantee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 25% of assessed tax (minimum WST 200); late payment interest of 2% per month, compounding; deliberate non-filing is prosecutable with a fine up to WST 50,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax on dividends paid by a resident Samoan company to non-residents; 0% on dividends and distributions paid by a tax-exempt International Company (no deduction at source because the IC has no Samoan tax liability).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's comprehensive double tax treaty network is minimal; relief is administered by the Ministry for Revenue on a payer-withholding basis. A claimant beneficial owner must submit: (i) Form DT-1 beneficial ownership declaration, (ii) a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the residence jurisdiction, and (iii) the IC's share register. Because an International Company's offshore distributions are already exempt, no TRC or treaty claim is required for outbound IC dividends; retain evidence of non-Samoan source to defeat any recharacterization.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding tax: interest 15%; royalties 15%. Treaty-reduced rates, where a DTA applies, range from 0% to 15%; IP royalties derived by an IC from licensing a baijiu brand internally are exempt from Samoan WHT provided the source is offshore and no Samoan-resident payer is involved.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No published statutory threshold in the Income Tax Act 2012; the MoR applies an indicative threshold of WST 5,000,000 aggregate annual related-party cross-border turnover above which contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation is required. A tax-exempt International Company sits outside the CIT net but must still document arm's-length export margins for its Economic Substance Declaration and to resist any recharacterization of income as Samoan-source.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations under the International Companies Act 2023 apply with full force. A baijiu export distribution IC is classified as a 'Distribution and Service Centre' relevant activity and must demonstrate: board meetings held in Samoa, physical premises in Samoa, qualified employees resident in Samoa, adequate local operating expenditure, and core income-generating activities performed in Samoa. An annual Economic Substance Declaration must be filed with SIFA; failure triggers penalties, deregistration, and recharacterization of the IC as a resident taxable company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Exemption Breach / Unauthorized Domestic Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC sells baijiu into the Samoan domestic market, employs Samoan-resident staff outside an approved structure, owns Samoan real property, or derives any Samoan-source income, thereby forfeiting the International Company tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive corporate income tax at 27% on all Samoan-source profits; penalty surcharge up to 100% of the tax evaded; interest at 2% per month compounding; assessment of 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions; strike-off by the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax after strike-off; courts may impose travel bans to secure collection; knowing breach is a criminal offence punishable by fine up to WST 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox entity with no registered-office substance, no active engagement of the licensed Samoa agent, no accounting records kept in Samoa, or filing a false Economic Substance Declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance penalties up to WST 100,000 per contravention; deregistration of the IC; automatic loss of the tax exemption; adverse notification to the Samoan FIU and international regulatory partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines for knowingly certifying false substance declarations; disqualification from acting as a director for up to 5 years; cross-border asset-freeze orders in aid of foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling large Swift-wire and letter-of-credit settlement flows for baijiu export without beneficial-owner due diligence, using personal accounts for corporate receipts, or structuring transactions to evade reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act: fines up to WST 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 14 years; asset forfeiture; FIU freezing orders against bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally prosecutable for willful blindness or consent to laundering; travel bans and passport surrender may be imposed pending investigation; civil confiscation of director assets traceable to tainted funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing fictitious export invoices (phantom baijiu shipments), inflating intercompany purchase prices to strip value from the IC, filing knowingly false annual returns, or trading while insolvent to defraud creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act 2023: criminal fine up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; restitution orders for funds extracted; voidability of fraudulent preferences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are civilly liable for the company's debts where fraudulent trading is proved (piercing the corporate veil); disqualification; court-ordered travel bans; extradition cooperation for related foreign offences.
